Indications and Contraindications of a Barium #6

  • Examination:
  • A. Indications:
  • Findings of pathological or possibly pathological
  • conditions of the digestive tract during other imaging
  • procedures => assessment of the movements of the
  • digestive tract
  • Postoperative assessment of the morphology and
  • dynamics of digestive segments (Radioscopy still
  • represents the best method of physiological assessment)
  • Assessment of chronic digestive tract diseases
  • (suspicion of malformations, Inflammatory Bowel
  • Disease, ulcers, bowel tumors etc.)

B. Contraindications for Ba examinations: #7

  • B.1. Absolute:
  • suspicion of gastro-intestinal perforation
  • intestinal occlusion
  • B.2. Relative:
  • recent gastrointestinal hemorrhage
  • acute digestive diseases
  • pregnancy (esp. in the first 3 mo)
  • altered general state

2. Native (“plain”) radiologic examination #8

  • of the abdomen.
  • Main purpose:
  • • quick diagnosis of acute conditions
  • • contraindications of Ba administration
  • • associated abdominal pathology or
  • complications

Intestinal Occlusion #13

  • Pozitive diagnosis
  • Evidence of hydro-aeric levels (could be
  • missing – false negative Dx).
  • In dynamic ileuses, the distention by gas is
  • the main component, in mechanical ileuses
  • the liquid buildup is the main component.

Preparation for the radiological examination of the bowel #21

  • 1. Bowel preparation per se
  • Upper GI tract:
  • – NO food, liquids or smoking in the morning of the examination.
  • – Time of examination: best between 8-10 a.m. (to prevent gastric
  • hypersecretion due to hunger)
  • – Evacuation of stasis liquid for patients with gastric stasis
  • Small Bowel: Hydric diet and purgatives in the day of examination
  • Colon: Fasting, purgation (the day before) + high evacuation enemas
  • 2. Premedication with farmacodynamic substances
  • They have specific indications in the exploration of the small bowel.
  • Are either hypotonic (glucagon or methylscopolamin), or accelerate the
  • intestinal transit (metoclopramid).

ACHALASIA #28

  • DEFINITION:
  • • incomplete relaxation or lack of relaxation of the lower esophageal
  • sphincter (LES) during deglutition
  • • absence of primary peristaltic waves in the lower 2/3
  • • hypertonic LES at rest
  • FUCTIONAL CHANGES
  • • lack of peristalsis in the lower 2/3 of the esophagus
  • • non-peristaltic, non-propulsive contractions
  • • absence of LES relaxation – short axial stenosis: “bird beak” appearence
  • - lack of the stomach gas bubble, HA level in the esophagus
  • - sedimentation of Ba and food
  • ORGANIC CHANGES
  • • esophageal dilation (megaesophagus)
  • • lengthening of the esophagus (megadolicoesophagus)
